name: releases-latest-null-digest
description: SPECIAL CASE, NEGATIVE (not a wire fixture — no `wire`/`expect` envelope, its own loader on both sides). The same captured `releases/latest` shape as 11-releases-latest.json, but the setup-exe asset carries `"digest": null`. This is a REAL GitHub state, not a hypothetical: the per-asset `digest` field only started being populated on 2025-06-03, so any asset uploaded before that date returns null, and a re-uploaded or replaced asset can too. THE RULE BOTH PARSERS MUST IMPLEMENT (D-15): a missing or null digest is a HARD REFUSAL — the update fails with `update.progress {stage:"failed", error:"checksum"}` and nothing is downloaded, executed or installed. It is NEVER a skipped verification and NEVER a "download it anyway and trust the TLS transport". `expectRefusal` below names the exact D-11 error code the refusal must produce, which makes this an executable contract rather than a code comment. Rationale: the digest is the ONLY integrity check standing between a tampered asset and an installer run with the owner's privileges — treating its absence as permission to skip verification would silently disable the one defence that exists (SPEC §12).
